newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher in quiet dealings. March closed at $304.80 a gain of $4.00 on the day while May was up $3.30 at $304.40. In New York raw sugar futures consolidated recent losses and climbed to 8-week highs, buoyed by technically-driven short covering and a flurry of fresh speculative buying. March added 21 points to close at 10.77 cents/lb while May last traded 17 points higher at 10.81 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 14 and 18 points. There were no fundamental factors behind the rise and the outlook remains bearish.

RUSSIA - According to industry sources sugar production in Russia in 1996/97 will reach only 1.654 million tonnes, white value, down from 2.06 million tonnes last year and far short of domestic demand estimated at around 5 million tonnes. As already reported sugar beet production this year will be around 16 million tonnes, down from 19.1 million tonnes the previous year. It was added that refineries will produce an additional 1.5 million tonnes of white sugar from imported raws, half a million tonnes more than last year. This is still below capacity put at 3.5 million tonnes. However, the Russian sugar industry is optimistic that sugar beet production will rise again and the total is estimated to reach 32.7 million tonnes by the end of the century and 37.8 million tonnes by the year 2005. Sugar production in 2000 is forecast to reach 3.2 million tonnes and 4 million tonnes by 2005.

GERMANY - The Association of the German Sugar Industry WVZ raised its estimate for the 1996/97 beet crop to 25.962 million tonnes, 167,600 tonnes more than forecast earlier. The increase was mainly due to better yields in Lower Saxony and Bavaria. Sugar production in the week ended December 13 amounted to 305,468 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 287,789 tonnes and the 1994 result of 144,682 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the 1996 campaign up to 4.307 million tonnes against 3.977 million tonnes in 1995 and 3.920 million tonnes in 1994. The total amount of beet processed so far reached 24.920 million tonnes which is 96 per cent of the estimated total.

TAIWAN - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 31,500 tonnes, raw value, against negligible amounts in the same month the previous year. This brought cumulative imports in the first eleven months of 1995/96 (November/September) up to 92,576 tonnes against 93,886 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 125,386 tonnes compared to 32,774 tonnes in 1993/94. The major country of origin in November/September 1996 was Australia with 92,500 tonnes raws. Cumulative sugar exports in November/September reached 25,559 tonnes, up from 14,772 tonnes in 1994/95. Total export in 1994/95 reached 14,782 tonnes against 13,338 tonnes in 1993/94. The major country of destination in November/September 1995/96 was the USA with 25,532 tonnes raws.

IRELAND - Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 3,859 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 67,360 tonnes compared to 45,959 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 reached 56,773 tonnes, up from 31,867 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were the United Kingdom with 36,703 tonnes whites against 35,298 tonnes, Israel with 11,635 tonnes, up from 6,515 tonnes and Turkey with 9,999 tonnes against nil.
F.O. LICHT - Our second estimate of European beet sugar production 1996/97 will be released on December 18, 1400 hrs central European time.
